# raseeda

> raseeda is a free, private invoice generator that runs entirely in the browser. There is no account and nothing is uploaded: invoices are saved in the browser on the user's device (IndexedDB), the PDF is made on the device, and invoice content leaves it only in files the user saves. The site counts anonymous usage (event names, country, browser family, OS, device type, language, the kind of site a visit came from, and a few bucketed invoice details such as the currency code, never names or amounts) with no cookies or identifiers. It is open source under the MIT licence.

## Pages

- [Home](https://raseeda.com/): what raseeda does, how it compares with other invoice generators and accounting software, what goes on the invoice, and common questions
- [Invoice editor](https://raseeda.com/create): create, edit and download an invoice as an A4 or Letter PDF (requires JavaScript)
- [Invoice templates](https://raseeda.com/invoice-template): sample invoices for freelance, consulting, small business, contractor, photography and web development work, each opening the editor in its font
- [Privacy](https://raseeda.com/privacy): what raseeda stores, where, and what never leaves the device

## Facts

- Free, with no paid plan, no ads and no watermark on the PDF.
- No account and no sign-up.
- Invoices, quotes, proforma invoices, receipts and credit notes, each with its own title and labels.
- Any currency, VAT or sales tax, fees, discounts, payment details (bank, account and routing numbers, IBAN, BIC / SWIFT, sort code, each under a label you can rename, and other ways to pay such as PayPal, Venmo, Pix or UPI), templates for repeat clients, and import / export backups.
- raseeda makes the PDF; it does not email invoices or track payments.
- No server API and no server-side storage. In the editor, `window.raseeda` offers an on-device API for scripts and assistants driving the browser: `listInvoices()`, `getInvoice(id)`, `createInvoice(data)`, `openInvoice(id)`, `getPdf(id?)`, `downloadPdf(id?)` and `importData(json)`. Invoice data takes the shape of an export's `invoiceData`; `documentType` (`"invoice"`, `"quote"`, `"proforma-invoice"`, `"receipt"` or `"credit-note"`, `"invoice"` when left out) sets the default title, sample number (`"QUO-0001"`, `"CN-0001"` and so on) and the number, due date and total labels (a quote's due date reads "Valid until", a receipt's "Date paid", a credit note's total "Total credit"); with `tax.perLine` on, an item's own `tax: { percentage, exempt }` overrides the invoice's rate. `tableSettings.columns` (`{ quantityAndPrice, unit }`) switches the Quantity, Unit and Unit price columns off, and `tableSettings.columnLabels.tax` names the Tax column (blank uses the tax row's label) and `columnLabels.amount` the Amount column (blank reads "Net amount" with tax on, "Amount" without). `numberFormat` (`"comma-dot"`, `"dot-comma"`, `"space-comma"`, `"apostrophe-dot"` or `"indian"`) and `currencyPosition` (`"before"` or `"after"`) say how amounts are written; `paperSize` (`"A4"` or `"Letter"`) is the page size. Left out, a script's invoice is `"comma-dot"`, `"before"` and `"A4"`. Zero-decimal currencies such as JPY are reckoned in whole units. `paymentDetails.labels` renames the bank fields (`routingNumber: "BSB"`) and `paymentDetails.methods` (`[{ id, name, detail }]`) lists other ways to pay, printed below them; `paymentDetails.paymentLink` is a link to pay online, printed last and clickable in the PDF. Documented in the README.
